notes: Independent manual audit at the pinned commit: read Inspector root AGENTS.md, benchmark contract and entire README, source root/extensions/SDK instructions, source plugin metadata, and every eligible production file. No Inspector implementation, detector output, helpers, or other plugin fixtures were read. Findings and usage sites were manually authored; scripting only serializes them, takes exact preselected evidence lines, and computes inventory/hashes.

All production local static and dynamic imports remain beneath extensions/file-transfer. The local shared/ and node-host/ source, lazy tool modules, CLI migration, doctor-contract-api.ts and embedded Node worker strings are included. There is no additional plugin-owned/shared shipped source beyond the root. Public SDK facade/type definitions were consulted for provenance only; their implementations and separately installed @openclaw/fs-safe, minimatch, typebox and commander dependencies are outside the audit population.

The package declares index.ts as its sole extension entry. This is a source-phase audit: eligible source is included even without runtime reachability. package.json itself adds no SDK syntactic or manifest-contract identity; its @openclaw/plugin-sdk devDependency is not an openclaw/plugin-sdk import.

The test-api.ts barrel and both test-support files were read and their callers verified. They remain excluded because only test suites/test barrels use them. Worker command source strings contain node: built-ins only, with no SDK module site or hook registration.

Original aliases are preserved: security-runtime root is imported as fsRoot in node-host/dir-fetch.ts; runtime-config-snapshot readRuntimeConfig is imported as getRuntimeConfig in shared/policy.ts. Identically named exports from different public SDK subpaths remain distinct canonical identities.

OpenClawPluginApi is proven by explicit type annotations and definePluginEntry register typing. runtime.agent.resolveAgentWorkspaceDir is called directly through api.runtime. workspace-bridge.ts:39 explicitly indexes OpenClawPluginApi["runtime"]["nodes"]["invoke"], contributing a type-only runtime.nodes.invoke finding. workspace-service.ts:85-96 passes separately scoped ctx.invokeNode into options.invoke; plugin-registration.types.ts declares that service capability separately using Omit of runtime parameter types. Its invocation at workspace-bridge.ts:62 does not become a runtime call. Service context fields, policy ctx.approvals/invokeNode, node-host IO and PluginRuntime-shaped function signatures otherwise remain separate contracts, not API/runtime handle aliases.

Members of SDK helper return values (fs-safe root handles, prompt objects, deferred promises, media receipts and workspace access adapters) are not PluginRuntime members. The audit records each directly imported SDK export and actual call/type use without following helper internal effects. AgentWorkspaceAccess/SandboxFsBridge projections supply export type references, not PluginRuntime paths.

Explicit typeof uses make readConfigFileSnapshotForWrite, readWorkspaceSkillResources and security-runtime root mixed; FsSafeError is mixed because of direct class type annotations. Their modules retain runtime classification because all module import sites for those respective modules are value imports. Archive and plugin-entry have mixed module syntax because inline/type-only imports coexist with value imports.

Manifest contracts include only cliCommands.name and the four contracts.tools entries. doctorContract.configRepair, activation, categories, descriptive/config schema metadata and runtime node command strings are not agreed manifest-contract fields or named hooks. There are no api.on/registerHook calls and no genuinely unresolved SDK/API/runtime accesses.
